title: Taxes and Financial Constraints: Evidence from Linguistic Cues

scopes.description: Complete author-documented workflow for the paper and supplied Internet Appendix; the imported package does not contain a runnable workflow.

requirements.description: Data inputs for reproducing the main paper and supplemental empirical analyses. The Internet Appendix describes some source products and reports regression results, but the package does not specify the complete author workflow, input products, fields, identifiers, coverage, transformations, or acquisition routes.

issues.description: The imported author package contains only the Internet Appendix PDF. No runnable program or entry point is supplied, so the full author workflow cannot be attempted from this variant.

The appendix reports multiple empirical analyses and describes selected historical source products, but supplies no run instructions, program-to-output mapping, full data and variable specifications, preparation steps, generated intermediates, software requirements, or execution logs. Required inputs and dependency closure therefore remain unknown; no analysis-only route is supported by the supplied materials.

evidence.description: The frozen work item inventories one material file, the Internet Appendix PDF, with no supplied data/code files, no dependency checklist entries, and no related package candidates.
The static audit identifies one document, no entry points or dependency edges, and reports no supported code.

The Internet Appendix describes an empirical bank-loan analysis using historical DealScan and FDIC information and reports its results, but does not provide the executable workflow or complete replication inputs.
evidence.quote: We analyze the association of the number of failed banks in firms’ headquarter states and the associated loan spreads of carrying out bank loans in Internet Appendix Table 1. The data are obtained from the Loan Pricing Corporation’s DealScan database, a dataset contains detailed pricing information and contract terms of primarily syndicated loans provide by banks and various financial institutions.

actions.description: Request the missing author workflow and complete input specification before assessing feasibility or attempting replication.
steps: Obtain the complete author-provided replication materials for this package variant, including runnable programs, README or data description, supplied analysis data or documented authorized acquisition routes, and any execution logs.

Ask the authors to map every main-paper and Internet Appendix output to its entry point and document required input products, fields, identifiers, periods, transformations, manual preparation, generated files and producer order, software, and any data-sharing limits or approved alternatives.
Treat historical source references in the appendix as leads only; verify their exact role and compatibility against the supplied author workflow before recording them as live input routes.
validation: After the materials arrive, trace all entry points and branches to the documented outputs and account for every required input and intermediate.
Use bounded metadata and software probes to check specified input formats, fields, periods, and runtimes; record unresolved access or coverage conditions.
Only after workflow closure, schedule an authorized run using the author-prescribed command and compare outputs with the cited tables; the current package provides no command to run.

review_notes: Assessment is limited to the imported package variant: its only material file is the Internet Appendix PDF. The dependency checklist is empty, but that does not establish workflow closure because no author program or run specification is supplied.
The appendix describes selected historical sources for supplemental analyses, but this is not a complete live input inventory or verified acquisition route. No independent reconstruction is proposed.
